ives-diary.author: George Cecil Ives
ives-diary.title: Diary (George Ives Papers, Harry Ransom Center, University of Texas at Austin)
ives-diary.note: Manuscript Collection MS-02138, eadid 00060; Series III. Diaries, 1886-1949, 122 volumes, open for research. Most volumes carry daily entries from 20 December 1886 to 16 November 1949 - **note the diaries END in November 1949, not 1950**, though Ives lived to 4 June 1950. Repo transcript covers 21 and 23 Nov 1906 only (transcription by Brian Lewis, personal communication). Other diary passages must be quoted via the secondary work that prints them (Cook, Kaplan, Stokes, Lewis), cited at that work's page. TARGETING (finding aid read 2026-08-05): **Cook's volume numbers ARE the Center's volume numbers** - his endnote 62 cites vol. 76 for 14 September 1920, and the container list gives v.76 as 2 September - 24 October 1920 - so every diary citation in Cook's endnotes (printed 125-131) converts directly into a requestable container. Bloodworth's 1909 arrival falls in v.51-55 (6 November 1907 - 14 June 1911); the 1939 will falls in v.104 (28 March 1939 - 18 March 1940) on either of Cook's two conflicting dates for it, October or 1 December 1939. Volumes 1-60 are bound in groups of five and 'bound very tightly and require special care when opening', which constrains reproduction. Ives INDEXED every volume from vol. 13 on, each index pointing to that volume's own page numbers - so the cheap way into an undated question is the index pages, not the volumes. Ives also wrote in several codes; see 'A Catalogue of the George Ives Collection', an appendix to the inventory. The address book (box 5, folder 8) 'provides cross references to his diaries'.

troubridge-diaries-hrc.author: Una Vincenzo, Lady Troubridge
troubridge-diaries-hrc.title: Diaries (Radclyffe Hall and Una Vincenzo, Lady Troubridge Collection, Harry Ransom Center)
troubridge-diaries-hrc.note: Unpublished; cite by entry date. Manuscript Collection MS-01793, eadid 00163. **131 volumes is the COMBINED total across two series, not Series II alone** (an earlier note here double-counted): Series II holds the 60-volume set running 27 December 1930 to 21 June 1943, containers 26.1-32.4; Series III holds 71 further volumes, 11 December 1943 to 21 January 1951, boxes 38-45 (formerly numbered 1-8, which is where the stray '8 boxes' came from). THE TWO SERIES ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE: the Series III volumes were written as letters to Hall AFTER her death on 7 October 1943, so they evidence Troubridge's grief and the estate, not the partnership in life. Note also that the diaries begin only in December 1930, fifteen years into a partnership that started in 1915 - they cannot speak to its first half at all. Supplemented by daybooks for 1934, 1935, 1941 and 1942 (Container 33.1 onward). Condition: 'Some materials in Series I. and II. are extensively water damaged, suffering rust and mold.' Access: open, but researchers must create an online account. Same repository as ives-diary - a natural add-on to the Ives fellowship trip. TARGETING (finding aid read 2026-08-05): Vol. 1 (Container 26.1) opens the diary and states its purpose; Vol. 22, 14 June - 9 October 1934 (Container 28.3) covers the start of the Souline affair, Hall's letters to Souline beginning July 1934; Vol. 60, 6 February - 21 June 1943 (Container 32.4) is the last before Hall's death. Troubridge's own 68 letters to Souline, 1934-1942, are Container 50.5-6. **Not itemised in the container list but described in the scope note, and the single most relevant document to this pair**: a letter 'To the Executors of my Will', written by Troubridge February 1944 and revised September 1944, 'regarding the nature of Troubridge and Hall's relationship with Souline and instructions for the destruction of Troubridge's diaries'. Container 36.1 is the likeliest home; ask the Center to locate it by name.

_voice_note: Quotes carry a per-quote `voice`: 'period' when the text is ENTIRELY in the words of someone alive in the world this map describes (a letter, a diary, sworn testimony, a contemporary memoir or interview), 'modern' when a historian, biographer or editor is writing about them. It is deliberately per-quote, not per-work: Holland & Hart-Davis's footnotes are modern prose inside a primary volume, while a Douglas or Langtry letter printed inside one of those same footnotes is still a period voice. Mixed text - a biographer's sentence with a period phrase quoted inside it - counts as modern, because it is not entirely the period voice. The panel sets period quotes between large quotation marks; modern ones keep a plain rule.
_evidence_date_note: A source's `evidence_date` is the date of the THING BEING EVIDENCED - when the letter was written, the testimony sworn, the meeting held - never the publication year of the book it is quoted from. A 1985 biography describing an 1908 holiday carries 1908. The panel orders a connection's sources by this field, so a publication year files modern commentary among the contemporary record. Where a card evidences no dated event at all - historiography, a statement about how a claim is treated in scholarship - leave it null; undated cards sort to the end.

116 pp, text-layered but the layer is BADLY CORRUPT - it renders 'like' as 'Hke', 'little' as 'Httle', 'delicate' as 'dehcate'. Use it to find; transcribe only from the rendered page.
THIS IS THE FIRST-EDITION TEXT. Its copyright page states 'French text printed by Alphonse Lemerre, Paris, 1904', and Dagmar is present throughout (39 occurrences) - so it translates the 1904 original, not the 1905 rewrite. Translation © 1976, this printing 1982. It unblocks what had been blocked since 2026-08-03: the 1904 French is still unobtained, but its content is now readable. Quotations from it are Foster's English, not Vivien's French - flag that in provenance and do not treat the wording as Vivien's own.
Gayle Rubin's introduction is a substantial piece of scholarship in its own right and identifies the roman-a-clef cast independently of Parker.

vivien-une-femme-1905-repo.author: Renée Vivien
vivien-une-femme-1905-repo.title: Une femme m'apparut…
vivien-une-femme-1905-repo.short_cite: Vivien, Une femme m'apparut… (1905 nouvelle édition)
vivien-une-femme-1905-repo.note:
208 pp, text-layered and the layer is good (French accents intact). It IS the French - but it is the 1905 rewrite, NOT the 1904 first edition, and the book says so itself: the title page at PDF p. 19, read as a page image 2026-08-04, reads 'Une Femme m'apparut. / NOUVELLE ÉDITION / PARIS / ALPHONSE LEMERRE, ÉDITEUR / 23-31, PASSAGE CHOISEUL / M DCCCCV'. A HardPress reprint of a Boston Public Library copy digitised by the Internet Archive; the '1877' in the filename is Vivien's birth year, not an edition date.
The cast confirms it independently: Lorély (165 occurrences), Ione, Nedda, Doriane, Undine, San Giovanni - and no Dagmar in any spelling. Lorély is the 1905's replacement for the 1904's Vally, so her presence is positive evidence for the rewrite rather than mere absence of Dagmar. NOTE FOR SEARCHING: 'Lorély' carries an acute accent and an unaccented grep for 'Lorely' returns nothing - that briefly made this copy look like it had no leading lady at all.
For Dagmar use vivien-foster-1982, whose copyright page states it translates the Lemerre 1904.
OPEN DISCREPANCY, 2026-08-04. This scanned 1905 runs to printed p. 168 and contains no Dagmar chapters - an accent- and OCR-tolerant search of all 208 pages finds no 'dagmar', 'poetesse', 'saxe' or 'ressentais', while distinctive phrases elsewhere in the book are found normally, so it is not a search failure. But the French Wikisource text explicitly labelled 1905 (fr.wikisource.org/wiki/Une_femme_m'apparut/1905, in the Anna's Archive EPUB in this folder) has Lorély 207 times AND Dagmar 32 times, in chapters XXXV-XXXVIII. Both cannot be right. Either this printed copy is shorter than the text Wikisource transcribed, or Wikisource's 1905 is conflated. Until that is resolved, do not repeat the flat claim that Dagmar appears only in the 1904 - what IS established is that she is absent from this printed 1905 copy and present in the 1904.
